Concerning its amount the exegetes have four opinions. One: a monthly yield after a month, said by Umar ibn al-Khattab. Two: a thousand dinars, said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ibn Jubayr. Al-Farra' said: "We see that "mamdud" was made the limit of the number, because "alf" (thousand) is the limit of the number, returning at the beginning of the count from the thousand." Three: four thousand, said by Qatadah. Four: that it was a garden he had in al-Ta'if whose produce never ceased in winter or summer, said by Muqatil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And sons present﴾, that is, they were present with him, not needing to travel for business and thus be absent from him. Concerning their number there are four opinions. One: ten, said by Mujahid and Qatadah. Two: thirteen, said by Ibn Jubayr. Three: twelve, said by al-Suddi. Four: seven, said by Muqatil. ﴿And I made smooth for him a smoothing﴾, that is, I spread out for him life and long life. "Then he hopes that I will increase him" — concerning this there are two opinions. One: he hopes that I will admit him to Paradise, said by al-Hasan. Two: that I will increase him in wealth and children, said by Muqatil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No!﴾, that is, I will not do that. So Allah withheld from him wealth and children until he died poor. ﴿Indeed, he was stubborn toward Our verses﴾, that is, opposing.

Concerning the meaning of "verses" here there are three opinions. One: it is the Qur'an, said by Ibn Jubayr. Two: the truth, said by Mujahid. Three: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said by al-Suddi.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I will drive him to a arduous climb﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: I will load him with a hardship of punishment. Others said: I will burden him with a hardship of punishment from which he will have no relief. Ibn Qutaybah said: "al-Su'ud" is the difficult ascent, and likewise "al-Ka'ud." In the hadith of Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I will drive him to a arduous climb﴾, he said: "A mountain of fire which he is commanded to climb; when he places his foot on it, it melts, and when he lifts it, it returns. He climbs for seventy autumns, then falls down in it, and so forever."

Ibn al-Sa'ib mentioned that it is a mountain of smooth rock in the Fire, which he is commanded to climb until, when he reaches its top, he is cast down to its bottom, then he is commanded to climb it again; this is his constant state forever, dragging chains of iron from in front of him and being struck with iron maces from behind him, so he climbs it over forty years.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, he reflected﴾, that is, he pondered what to say about the Qur'an. ﴿And he determined﴾, the statement within himself. ﴿So may he be destroyed, how he determined!﴾ ﴿Then may he be destroyed, how he determined!﴾, that is, may he be cursed in whatever state he determined what he determined of speech. It was also said: "how" here means astonishment, denial, and rebuke. It was repeated for emphasis. ﴿Then he looked﴾ for means to repel and refute the Qur'an. ﴿Then he frowned and scowled﴾. The linguists said: that is, he contracted his face and knitted his brow. It is said: "basara al-rajul wajhahu," meaning he tightened it. They cited Tawbah's verse:
"Her aversion has troubled me, which I have seen, and her turning away from my need and her scowling."
The exegetes said: he made his face sour and looked with intense displeasure, like one anxious and deep in thought about a matter. ﴿Then he turned away﴾ from faith, ﴿and was arrogant﴾, that is, he was proud when invited to it. ﴿So he said: "This is not but magic transmitted"﴾, that is, this Qur'an is nothing but magic that is narrated from sorcerers. ﴿This is not but the word of a human﴾, that is, the speech of mankind, not the speech of Allah, exalted is He. So Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿I will drive him into Saqar﴾, that is, I will admit him into the Fire. Saqar was mentioned in [al-Qamar: 48]. ﴿And what can make you know what Saqar is?﴾ due to its great severity. ﴿It leaves nothing and spares nothing﴾, that is, it leaves none of their flesh without consuming it, and it spares none of them when they are restored in a new creation. ﴿Burning the skin﴾, that is, changing it. It is said: "laheth al-shams" meaning the sun altered him. They cited:
"O daughter of my uncle, the noontide heats have altered me."
Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn al-Sumayfa', and Ibn Abi Ablah read "lawwahatan" in the accusative. Concerning "al-bashar" there are two opinions. One: it is the plural of "bashrah," the outer skin of a person, said by Mujahid, al-Farra', and al-Zajjaj. Two: they are humans among the people of the Fire, said by al-Akhfash and Ibn Qutaybah among others.

His saying, ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾: they are its guardians. Malik is their leader, and with him are eighteen. Their eyes are like flashing lightning, their fangs are like tusks, and flames of fire come out of their mouths. [p. 408] The distance between the shoulders of each one of them is a year's journey. The palm of one of them could hold the like of Rabi'ah and Mudar. Mercy has been removed from them.

When this verse was revealed, Abu Jahl said: "Muhammad frightens you with nineteen. Does he not have soldiers other than these? Will each ten of you be unable to overpower one of them, and then they will come out of the Fire?" Abu al-Ashaddayn said. Muqatil said: his name was Usayd ibn Kilda. Others said: Kalda ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi: "O assembly of Quraysh, I will walk before you, and I will lift ten with my right shoulder and nine with my left shoulder, and we will enter Paradise." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels﴾, not human beings. So who can withstand them, and who can overpower them? ﴿And We have not made their number﴾, in this small quantity, ﴿except as a trial﴾, that is, a misguidance ﴿for those who disbelieved﴾, to the extent that they said what they said. ﴿That those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾ that what Muhammad brought is true, because their number in the Torah is nineteen. ﴿And those who believed may increase in faith﴾ from among the People of the Book, ﴿in faith﴾, that is, in confirming Muhammad ﷺ, when they found that what he reports agrees with what is in their own Scripture. ﴿And those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt﴾, that is, these will not doubt the number of the guardians. ﴿And so that those in whose hearts is disease﴾ and in this there are three opinions.

The first: it is hypocrisy. This was mentioned by most scholars.

The second: it is doubt. This was said by Muqatil, who claimed that they were the Jews of Medina, and in his view this verse is Medinan.

[p. 409] The third: it is dissent. This was said by al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl, who said: "There was no hypocrisy in Mecca, and this is a Meccan surah." As for ﴿the disbelievers﴾, they are the polytheists of the Arabs. ﴿What did Allah intend﴾, that is, what thing did Allah intend ﴿by this﴾ report and account ﴿as an example﴾? The word "example" may mean the same as the account itself. The meaning of the speech is: they say, "What is this account?" ﴿Thus﴾, that is, just as He misguides whoever denies the number of the guardians and guides whoever confirms it, ﴿Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl's saying, "Does Muhammad not have soldiers other than nineteen?": ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾, meaning from among the angels whom He created to punish the people of the Fire. This is because each one of these nineteen has helpers that none knows except Allah.

Al-Mawardi mentioned, regarding the wisdom behind their being nineteen, a plausible opinion. He said: "Nineteen is a number that combines the greatest part of the few and the least part of the many, because single digits are the least of numbers, and the largest of them is nine, while everything beyond single digits is many. The least of many is ten. So it was limited to a number that combines the least of many and the greatest of few."

Then He returned to mention the Fire, and said the Exalted: ﴿And it is not except a reminder﴾, that is, the Fire in this world is only a reminder of the Fire of the Hereafter. ﴿No!﴾, that is, truly. ﴿By the moon﴾ ﴿And the night when it turns back﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr on the authority of 'Asim read ﴿idha adbara﴾ ("when it turns back"). Nafi', Hamzah, Hafs, al-Mufaddal on the authority of 'Asim, and Ya'qub read ﴿idh adbara﴾ with the dhal sukun, without an alif after it, and the dal sukun, with a hamza before it. Is the meaning of the two recitations (qira'at, recitational variants) the same or not? There are two opinions.

One: they are two dialects with the same meaning. It is said: "dabara al-layl" and "adbara" (the night turned back), and "dabara al-sayf" and "adbara" (the summer turned back). This is the view of al-Farra', al-Akhfash, and Tha'lab.

[p. 410] The second: "dabara" means "came after," and "adbara" means "turned away." It is said: "dabarani fulan" (so-and-so came behind me). This meaning was adopted by Abu 'Ubaydah and Ibn Qutaybah.

His saying, ﴿when it brightens﴾, that is, shines and becomes clear. ﴿Indeed, it is﴾, meaning Saqar, ﴿one of the greatest [calamities]﴾. Ibn Qutaybah said: "al-kubar" is the plural of "kubra," like "al-uwal" and "al-ula," and "al-sughar" and "al-sughra." This is like saying, "Indeed, it is one of the great matters." Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, Allah has never warned with anything more frightening than this."

Ibn al-Sa'ib and Muqatil said: by "al-kubar" He meant the seven levels of Hell.

His saying, ﴿a warning to humanity﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the accusative of "nadhiran" is in the position of a circumstantial state. The meaning is: indeed, it is great in the state of warning. "Nadhir" is masculine because its meaning is the meaning of punishment. It is also permissible for "nadhiran" to be in the accusative and connected to the beginning of the surah, in the sense of: "Arise as a warner to humanity."

His saying, ﴿for whoever among you wills﴾, is a substitute for His saying, ﴿to humanity﴾, ﴿to advance or to lag behind﴾. In this there are four opinions.

One: to advance in obedience to Allah or to lag behind from His disobedience. This was said by Ibn Juraij.

The second: to advance toward the Fire or to lag behind from Paradise. This was said by al-Suddi.

The third: to advance in goodness or to lag behind toward evil. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The fourth: to advance in faith or to lag behind from it. The meaning is that the warning has reached every person, whether he affirmed or disbelieved.

Surah 74: Al-Muddaththir

It is Meccan, by the consensus of scholars.

Muqatil said: Among it is one Medinan verse, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31].

As for the occasion of its revelation, al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated in their Sahihayn, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told us: "I was secluding myself in Hira for a month. When I had completed my seclusion, I descended and went into the valley's bottom, and I was called. I looked before me, behind me, to my right, and to my left, and I saw no one. Then I was called again, so I raised my head, and behold, he was in the air" — meaning Jibril (peace be upon him) — "so I came to Khadijah and said: 'Cover me, cover me!' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ ﴿Arise and warn﴾."

The exegetes said: When he saw Jibril, he fell unconscious. When he recovered, he entered upon Khadijah and asked for water, poured it over himself, and said: "Cover me!" So they covered him with a qatifah (a thick cloak). Then Jibril came to him and said: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu Imran, and al-A'mash read "al-mutadaththir" with the taa' made apparent. Abu Raja', Ikrimah, and Ibn Ya'mar read "al-mudaththir" with the taa' omitted and the dal lightened. The linguists said: The original form of "al-muddaththir" is "al-mutadaththir," and the taa' was assimilated into the dal, as we mentioned regarding "al-muzzammil." According to the majority, this is from tadthir (wrapping oneself) with garments. It was also said the meaning is: O you who are cloaked with prophethood and its burdens. Ikrimah said: You have been clothed with this matter, so arise and bear it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Arise and warn﴾: warn the disbelievers of Makkah of the punishment if they do not affirm Allah's oneness. ﴿And your Lord, glorify﴾: that is, exalt Him above what the idol-worshippers say. ﴿And your garments, purify﴾: concerning this there are eight opinions.

The first: Do not wear them in disobedience, nor in treachery. Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi said:
"And by Allah's praise, I have never worn a garment of an immoral man, nor do I veil myself with treachery."
Ikrimah narrated this meaning from Ibn Abbas.

The second: Let your garments not be from unlawful earnings. This is also narrated from Ibn Abbas.

The third: Purify yourself from sin. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah. As evidence for it is the saying of Antarah:
"I pierced his garments with the stout spear, for the noble one is not made sacred by the spear-points."
That is, himself. This is the view of Ibn Qutaybah, who said: The meaning is: purify yourself from sins, and he referred to the body by garments, because they enclose it. Layla al-Akhyaliyyah said, describing camels:
"They threw upon them light garments, so you see them resembling nothing but the startled ostriches."
That is, they mounted them, throwing themselves upon them. The Arabs call chastity "izar" (a wrap), because the chaste person is, as it were, veiled by his chastity.

The fourth: And your deeds, make righteous. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The fifth: Your character, make good. This was said by al-Hasan and al-Qurazi.

The sixth: And your garments, shorten and tuck up. This was said by Tawus.

The seventh: Your heart, purify. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. As evidence for it is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:
"If my conduct has displeased you, then strip my garments from yours and you will be stripped."
That is, my heart from your heart.

The eighth: Wash your garments with water and cleanse them. This was said by Ibn Sirin and Ibn Zayd.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And uncleanness, abandon﴾. Al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Shaybah, Asim except Abu Bakr, Ya'qub, and Ibn Muhaysin, and Ibn al-Sumayfa' read "al-rujza" with a damma on the ra'. The rest read it with a kasra. They did not differ regarding any other place. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of both readings is one. Abu Ali said: The reading of al-Hasan is with the damma, and he said: it is the name of an idol. Qatadah said: They are two idols, Isaf and Na'ilah. Whoever reads with the kasra, then "al-rijz" means punishment, so the meaning is: "Possessor of punishment, abandon."

Concerning the meaning of "al-rijz" the exegetes have six opinions.

The first: It is the idols and images. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd.

The second: It is sin. This was also narrated from Ibn Abbas.

The third: It is polytheism. This was said by Ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak.

The fourth: It is sin. This was said by al-Hasan.

The fifth: It is punishment. This was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib. Al-Zajjaj said: "Al-rijz" in the language means punishment, and the meaning of the verse is: abandon whatever leads to Allah's punishment.

The sixth: It is Satan. This was said by Ibn Kaysan.

﴿And do not bestow favour seeking more﴾: concerning this there are four opinions.

The first: Do not give a gift seeking to receive something better than it. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Qatadah. The exegetes said: its meaning is: give for your Lord and intend by it Allah, so He disciplined him with the noblest manners. The meaning of "do not bestow favour" is: do not give some of your wealth in order to receive more than it. This manner is specific to the Prophet (ﷺ), and there is no sin upon any of his community who gives a gift hoping for a greater reward than it.

The second: Do not bestow favour by your deed, seeing it as great before your Lord. This was said by al-Hasan.

The third: Do not become weak in good, seeking to increase from it. This was said by Mujahid.

The fourth: Do not bestow favour upon people with prophethood in order to take a reward from them. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

﴿And for your Lord﴾: concerning this there are four opinions. The first: for the sake of your Lord. The second: for the reward of your Lord. The third: for the command of your Lord. The fourth: for the promise of your Lord. ﴿So be patient﴾: concerning this there are two opinions. One: in obeying Him and His obligations. The other: in the face of harm and denial.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when the trumpet is sounded﴾, that is, the Sur is blown. Is this blast the first or the second? Concerning this there are two opinions. ﴿That Day will be a difficult day﴾, that is, the matter will be hard on that Day. ﴿For the disbelievers, not easy﴾, not light. ﴿Leave Me﴾: we have explained this in [al-Muzzammil: 11]. ﴿And the one whom I created﴾, that is, the one whom I created ﴿alone﴾: concerning this there are two opinions.

One: I created him alone in his mother's womb, with no wealth and no children. This was said by Mujahid.

The second: I created him alone, with none sharing in his creation. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

Ibn Abbas said: "Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he recited the Qur'an to him, and he seemed to soften toward it. This reached Abu Jahl, so he came to him and said: 'O uncle, your people wish to gather wealth for you, for you came to Muhammad to seek what is in his hands.' He said: 'Quraysh knows that I am among the wealthiest of them.' He said: 'Then say something about him that will reach your people, that you deny him.' He said: 'And what should I say? By Allah, there is no man among you more knowledgeable in poetry than I am. By Allah, what he says does not resemble it. By Allah, his speech has sweetness, and it has radiance, its top is fruitful and its bottom is abundant, and it is high and nothing is above it.' He said: 'Your people will not be pleased with you until you say something about it.' He said: 'Leave me until I think about it.' Then he said: 'This is magic that is transmitted: he transmits it from others.' So the verses were revealed: ﴿Leave Me and the one whom I created alone...﴾ all of the verses."

Mujahid said: "Al-Walid said to Quraysh: 'I have a need of you.' So they gathered in the Council House (Dar al-Nadwah). He said: 'You are people of lineage and wisdom, and the Arabs come to you and depart from you with differing matters, so agree on one thing. What do you say about this man?' They said: 'We say he is a poet.' He frowned at that and said: 'We have heard poetry, and his speech does not resemble poetry.' They said: 'We say he is a soothsayer.' He said: 'Then they would come to him and find him not speaking as soothsayers speak.' They said: 'We say he is possessed.' He said: 'Then they would come to him and find him not possessed.' They said: 'We say he is a sorcerer.' He said: 'And what is a sorcerer?' They said: 'A human who makes beloved those who hate one another, and makes hateful those who love one another.' He said: 'Then he is a sorcerer.' So they went out, and no one among them met the Prophet without saying: 'O sorcerer!' This grieved him greatly, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ until His saying: ﴿This is nothing but magic transmitted.﴾"

Some exegetes mentioned that His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Leave Me and the one whom I created alone﴾ is abrogated by the verse of the sword, but this is not sound.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And I gave him extensive wealth﴾. Concerning the meaning of "mamdud" (extensive) there are three opinions. One: abundant, said by Abu Ubaydah. Two: perpetual, said by Ibn Qutaybah. Three: uninterrupted, said by al-Zajjaj.

Concerning its amount the exegetes have four opinions. One: a monthly yield after a month, said by Umar ibn al-Khattab. Two: a thousand dinars, said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ibn Jubayr. Al-Farra' said: "We see that "mamdud" was made the limit of the number, because "alf" (thousand) is the limit of the number, returning at the beginning of the count from the thousand." Three: four thousand, said by Qatadah. Four: that it was a garden he had in al-Ta'if whose produce never ceased in winter or summer, said by Muqatil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And sons present﴾, that is, they were present with him, not needing to travel for business and thus be absent from him. Concerning their number there are four opinions. One: ten, said by Mujahid and Qatadah. Two: thirteen, said by Ibn Jubayr. Three: twelve, said by al-Suddi. Four: seven, said by Muqatil. ﴿And I made smooth for him a smoothing﴾, that is, I spread out for him life and long life. "Then he hopes that I will increase him" — concerning this there are two opinions. One: he hopes that I will admit him to Paradise, said by al-Hasan. Two: that I will increase him in wealth and children, said by Muqatil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No!﴾, that is, I will not do that. So Allah withheld from him wealth and children until he died poor. ﴿Indeed, he was stubborn toward Our verses﴾, that is, opposing.

Concerning the meaning of "verses" here there are three opinions. One: it is the Qur'an, said by Ibn Jubayr. Two: the truth, said by Mujahid. Three: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said by al-Suddi.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I will drive him to a arduous climb﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: I will load him with a hardship of punishment. Others said: I will burden him with a hardship of punishment from which he will have no relief. Ibn Qutaybah said: "al-Su'ud" is the difficult ascent, and likewise "al-Ka'ud." In the hadith of Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I will drive him to a arduous climb﴾, he said: "A mountain of fire which he is commanded to climb; when he places his foot on it, it melts, and when he lifts it, it returns. He climbs for seventy autumns, then falls down in it, and so forever."

Ibn al-Sa'ib mentioned that it is a mountain of smooth rock in the Fire, which he is commanded to climb until, when he reaches its top, he is cast down to its bottom, then he is commanded to climb it again; this is his constant state forever, dragging chains of iron from in front of him and being struck with iron maces from behind him, so he climbs it over forty years.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, he reflected﴾, that is, he pondered what to say about the Qur'an. ﴿And he determined﴾, the statement within himself. ﴿So may he be destroyed, how he determined!﴾ ﴿Then may he be destroyed, how he determined!﴾, that is, may he be cursed in whatever state he determined what he determined of speech. It was also said: "how" here means astonishment, denial, and rebuke. It was repeated for emphasis. ﴿Then he looked﴾ for means to repel and refute the Qur'an. ﴿Then he frowned and scowled﴾. The linguists said: that is, he contracted his face and knitted his brow. It is said: "basara al-rajul wajhahu," meaning he tightened it. They cited Tawbah's verse:
"Her aversion has troubled me, which I have seen, and her turning away from my need and her scowling."
The exegetes said: he made his face sour and looked with intense displeasure, like one anxious and deep in thought about a matter. ﴿Then he turned away﴾ from faith, ﴿and was arrogant﴾, that is, he was proud when invited to it. ﴿So he said: "This is not but magic transmitted"﴾, that is, this Qur'an is nothing but magic that is narrated from sorcerers. ﴿This is not but the word of a human﴾, that is, the speech of mankind, not the speech of Allah, exalted is He. So Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿I will drive him into Saqar﴾, that is, I will admit him into the Fire. Saqar was mentioned in [al-Qamar: 48]. ﴿And what can make you know what Saqar is?﴾ due to its great severity. ﴿It leaves nothing and spares nothing﴾, that is, it leaves none of their flesh without consuming it, and it spares none of them when they are restored in a new creation. ﴿Burning the skin﴾, that is, changing it. It is said: "laheth al-shams" meaning the sun altered him. They cited:
"O daughter of my uncle, the noontide heats have altered me."
Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn al-Sumayfa', and Ibn Abi Ablah read "lawwahatan" in the accusative. Concerning "al-bashar" there are two opinions. One: it is the plural of "bashrah," the outer skin of a person, said by Mujahid, al-Farra', and al-Zajjaj. Two: they are humans among the people of the Fire, said by al-Akhfash and Ibn Qutaybah among others.

His saying, ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾: they are its guardians. Malik is their leader, and with him are eighteen. Their eyes are like flashing lightning, their fangs are like tusks, and flames of fire come out of their mouths. [p. 408] The distance between the shoulders of each one of them is a year's journey. The palm of one of them could hold the like of Rabi'ah and Mudar. Mercy has been removed from them.

When this verse was revealed, Abu Jahl said: "Muhammad frightens you with nineteen. Does he not have soldiers other than these? Will each ten of you be unable to overpower one of them, and then they will come out of the Fire?" Abu al-Ashaddayn said. Muqatil said: his name was Usayd ibn Kilda. Others said: Kalda ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi: "O assembly of Quraysh, I will walk before you, and I will lift ten with my right shoulder and nine with my left shoulder, and we will enter Paradise." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels﴾, not human beings. So who can withstand them, and who can overpower them? ﴿And We have not made their number﴾, in this small quantity, ﴿except as a trial﴾, that is, a misguidance ﴿for those who disbelieved﴾, to the extent that they said what they said. ﴿That those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾ that what Muhammad brought is true, because their number in the Torah is nineteen. ﴿And those who believed may increase in faith﴾ from among the People of the Book, ﴿in faith﴾, that is, in confirming Muhammad ﷺ, when they found that what he reports agrees with what is in their own Scripture. ﴿And those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt﴾, that is, these will not doubt the number of the guardians. ﴿And so that those in whose hearts is disease﴾ and in this there are three opinions.

The first: it is hypocrisy. This was mentioned by most scholars.

The second: it is doubt. This was said by Muqatil, who claimed that they were the Jews of Medina, and in his view this verse is Medinan.

[p. 409] The third: it is dissent. This was said by al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl, who said: "There was no hypocrisy in Mecca, and this is a Meccan surah." As for ﴿the disbelievers﴾, they are the polytheists of the Arabs. ﴿What did Allah intend﴾, that is, what thing did Allah intend ﴿by this﴾ report and account ﴿as an example﴾? The word "example" may mean the same as the account itself. The meaning of the speech is: they say, "What is this account?" ﴿Thus﴾, that is, just as He misguides whoever denies the number of the guardians and guides whoever confirms it, ﴿Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl's saying, "Does Muhammad not have soldiers other than nineteen?": ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾, meaning from among the angels whom He created to punish the people of the Fire. This is because each one of these nineteen has helpers that none knows except Allah.

Al-Mawardi mentioned, regarding the wisdom behind their being nineteen, a plausible opinion. He said: "Nineteen is a number that combines the greatest part of the few and the least part of the many, because single digits are the least of numbers, and the largest of them is nine, while everything beyond single digits is many. The least of many is ten. So it was limited to a number that combines the least of many and the greatest of few."

Then He returned to mention the Fire, and said the Exalted: ﴿And it is not except a reminder﴾, that is, the Fire in this world is only a reminder of the Fire of the Hereafter. ﴿No!﴾, that is, truly. ﴿By the moon﴾ ﴿And the night when it turns back﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr on the authority of 'Asim read ﴿idha adbara﴾ ("when it turns back"). Nafi', Hamzah, Hafs, al-Mufaddal on the authority of 'Asim, and Ya'qub read ﴿idh adbara﴾ with the dhal sukun, without an alif after it, and the dal sukun, with a hamza before it. Is the meaning of the two recitations (qira'at, recitational variants) the same or not? There are two opinions.

One: they are two dialects with the same meaning. It is said: "dabara al-layl" and "adbara" (the night turned back), and "dabara al-sayf" and "adbara" (the summer turned back). This is the view of al-Farra', al-Akhfash, and Tha'lab.

[p. 410] The second: "dabara" means "came after," and "adbara" means "turned away." It is said: "dabarani fulan" (so-and-so came behind me). This meaning was adopted by Abu 'Ubaydah and Ibn Qutaybah.

His saying, ﴿when it brightens﴾, that is, shines and becomes clear. ﴿Indeed, it is﴾, meaning Saqar, ﴿one of the greatest [calamities]﴾. Ibn Qutaybah said: "al-kubar" is the plural of "kubra," like "al-uwal" and "al-ula," and "al-sughar" and "al-sughra." This is like saying, "Indeed, it is one of the great matters." Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, Allah has never warned with anything more frightening than this."

Ibn al-Sa'ib and Muqatil said: by "al-kubar" He meant the seven levels of Hell.

His saying, ﴿a warning to humanity﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the accusative of "nadhiran" is in the position of a circumstantial state. The meaning is: indeed, it is great in the state of warning. "Nadhir" is masculine because its meaning is the meaning of punishment. It is also permissible for "nadhiran" to be in the accusative and connected to the beginning of the surah, in the sense of: "Arise as a warner to humanity."

His saying, ﴿for whoever among you wills﴾, is a substitute for His saying, ﴿to humanity﴾, ﴿to advance or to lag behind﴾. In this there are four opinions.

One: to advance in obedience to Allah or to lag behind from His disobedience. This was said by Ibn Juraij.

The second: to advance toward the Fire or to lag behind from Paradise. This was said by al-Suddi.

The third: to advance in goodness or to lag behind toward evil. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The fourth: to advance in faith or to lag behind from it. The meaning is that the warning has reached every person, whether he affirmed or disbelieved.

Surah 74: Al-Muddaththir

It is Meccan, by the consensus of scholars.

Muqatil said: Among it is one Medinan verse, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31].

As for the occasion of its revelation, al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated in their Sahihayn, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told us: "I was secluding myself in Hira for a month. When I had completed my seclusion, I descended and went into the valley's bottom, and I was called. I looked before me, behind me, to my right, and to my left, and I saw no one. Then I was called again, so I raised my head, and behold, he was in the air" — meaning Jibril (peace be upon him) — "so I came to Khadijah and said: 'Cover me, cover me!' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ ﴿Arise and warn﴾."

The exegetes said: When he saw Jibril, he fell unconscious. When he recovered, he entered upon Khadijah and asked for water, poured it over himself, and said: "Cover me!" So they covered him with a qatifah (a thick cloak). Then Jibril came to him and said: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu Imran, and al-A'mash read "al-mutadaththir" with the taa' made apparent. Abu Raja', Ikrimah, and Ibn Ya'mar read "al-mudaththir" with the taa' omitted and the dal lightened. The linguists said: The original form of "al-muddaththir" is "al-mutadaththir," and the taa' was assimilated into the dal, as we mentioned regarding "al-muzzammil." According to the majority, this is from tadthir (wrapping oneself) with garments. It was also said the meaning is: O you who are cloaked with prophethood and its burdens. Ikrimah said: You have been clothed with this matter, so arise and bear it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Arise and warn﴾: warn the disbelievers of Makkah of the punishment if they do not affirm Allah's oneness. ﴿And your Lord, glorify﴾: that is, exalt Him above what the idol-worshippers say. ﴿And your garments, purify﴾: concerning this there are eight opinions.

The first: Do not wear them in disobedience, nor in treachery. Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi said:
"And by Allah's praise, I have never worn a garment of an immoral man, nor do I veil myself with treachery."
Ikrimah narrated this meaning from Ibn Abbas.

The second: Let your garments not be from unlawful earnings. This is also narrated from Ibn Abbas.

The third: Purify yourself from sin. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah. As evidence for it is the saying of Antarah:
"I pierced his garments with the stout spear, for the noble one is not made sacred by the spear-points."
That is, himself. This is the view of Ibn Qutaybah, who said: The meaning is: purify yourself from sins, and he referred to the body by garments, because they enclose it. Layla al-Akhyaliyyah said, describing camels:
"They threw upon them light garments, so you see them resembling nothing but the startled ostriches."
That is, they mounted them, throwing themselves upon them. The Arabs call chastity "izar" (a wrap), because the chaste person is, as it were, veiled by his chastity.

The fourth: And your deeds, make righteous. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The fifth: Your character, make good. This was said by al-Hasan and al-Qurazi.

The sixth: And your garments, shorten and tuck up. This was said by Tawus.

The seventh: Your heart, purify. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. As evidence for it is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:
"If my conduct has displeased you, then strip my garments from yours and you will be stripped."
That is, my heart from your heart.

The eighth: Wash your garments with water and cleanse them. This was said by Ibn Sirin and Ibn Zayd.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And uncleanness, abandon﴾. Al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Shaybah, Asim except Abu Bakr, Ya'qub, and Ibn Muhaysin, and Ibn al-Sumayfa' read "al-rujza" with a damma on the ra'. The rest read it with a kasra. They did not differ regarding any other place. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of both readings is one. Abu Ali said: The reading of al-Hasan is with the damma, and he said: it is the name of an idol. Qatadah said: They are two idols, Isaf and Na'ilah. Whoever reads with the kasra, then "al-rijz" means punishment, so the meaning is: "Possessor of punishment, abandon."

Concerning the meaning of "al-rijz" the exegetes have six opinions.

The first: It is the idols and images. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd.

The second: It is sin. This was also narrated from Ibn Abbas.

The third: It is polytheism. This was said by Ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak.

The fourth: It is sin. This was said by al-Hasan.

The fifth: It is punishment. This was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib. Al-Zajjaj said: "Al-rijz" in the language means punishment, and the meaning of the verse is: abandon whatever leads to Allah's punishment.

The sixth: It is Satan. This was said by Ibn Kaysan.

﴿And do not bestow favour seeking more﴾: concerning this there are four opinions.

The first: Do not give a gift seeking to receive something better than it. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Qatadah. The exegetes said: its meaning is: give for your Lord and intend by it Allah, so He disciplined him with the noblest manners. The meaning of "do not bestow favour" is: do not give some of your wealth in order to receive more than it. This manner is specific to the Prophet (ﷺ), and there is no sin upon any of his community who gives a gift hoping for a greater reward than it.

The second: Do not bestow favour by your deed, seeing it as great before your Lord. This was said by al-Hasan.

The third: Do not become weak in good, seeking to increase from it. This was said by Mujahid.

The fourth: Do not bestow favour upon people with prophethood in order to take a reward from them. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

﴿And for your Lord﴾: concerning this there are four opinions. The first: for the sake of your Lord. The second: for the reward of your Lord. The third: for the command of your Lord. The fourth: for the promise of your Lord. ﴿So be patient﴾: concerning this there are two opinions. One: in obeying Him and His obligations. The other: in the face of harm and denial.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when the trumpet is sounded﴾, that is, the Sur is blown. Is this blast the first or the second? Concerning this there are two opinions. ﴿That Day will be a difficult day﴾, that is, the matter will be hard on that Day. ﴿For the disbelievers, not easy﴾, not light. ﴿Leave Me﴾: we have explained this in [al-Muzzammil: 11]. ﴿And the one whom I created﴾, that is, the one whom I created ﴿alone﴾: concerning this there are two opinions.

One: I created him alone in his mother's womb, with no wealth and no children. This was said by Mujahid.

The second: I created him alone, with none sharing in his creation. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

Ibn Abbas said: "Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he recited the Qur'an to him, and he seemed to soften toward it. This reached Abu Jahl, so he came to him and said: 'O uncle, your people wish to gather wealth for you, for you came to Muhammad to seek what is in his hands.' He said: 'Quraysh knows that I am among the wealthiest of them.' He said: 'Then say something about him that will reach your people, that you deny him.' He said: 'And what should I say? By Allah, there is no man among you more knowledgeable in poetry than I am. By Allah, what he says does not resemble it. By Allah, his speech has sweetness, and it has radiance, its top is fruitful and its bottom is abundant, and it is high and nothing is above it.' He said: 'Your people will not be pleased with you until you say something about it.' He said: 'Leave me until I think about it.' Then he said: 'This is magic that is transmitted: he transmits it from others.' So the verses were revealed: ﴿Leave Me and the one whom I created alone...﴾ all of the verses."

Mujahid said: "Al-Walid said to Quraysh: 'I have a need of you.' So they gathered in the Council House (Dar al-Nadwah). He said: 'You are people of lineage and wisdom, and the Arabs come to you and depart from you with differing matters, so agree on one thing. What do you say about this man?' They said: 'We say he is a poet.' He frowned at that and said: 'We have heard poetry, and his speech does not resemble poetry.' They said: 'We say he is a soothsayer.' He said: 'Then they would come to him and find him not speaking as soothsayers speak.' They said: 'We say he is possessed.' He said: 'Then they would come to him and find him not possessed.' They said: 'We say he is a sorcerer.' He said: 'And what is a sorcerer?' They said: 'A human who makes beloved those who hate one another, and makes hateful those who love one another.' He said: 'Then he is a sorcerer.' So they went out, and no one among them met the Prophet without saying: 'O sorcerer!' This grieved him greatly, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ until His saying: ﴿This is nothing but magic transmitted.﴾"

Some exegetes mentioned that His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Leave Me and the one whom I created alone﴾ is abrogated by the verse of the sword, but this is not sound.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And I gave him extensive wealth﴾. Concerning the meaning of "mamdud" (extensive) there are three opinions. One: abundant, said by Abu Ubaydah. Two: perpetual, said by Ibn Qutaybah. Three: uninterrupted, said by al-Zajjaj.

Concerning its amount the exegetes have four opinions. One: a monthly yield after a month, said by Umar ibn al-Khattab. Two: a thousand dinars, said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ibn Jubayr. Al-Farra' said: "We see that "mamdud" was made the limit of the number, because "alf" (thousand) is the limit of the number, returning at the beginning of the count from the thousand." Three: four thousand, said by Qatadah. Four: that it was a garden he had in al-Ta'if whose produce never ceased in winter or summer, said by Muqatil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And sons present﴾, that is, they were present with him, not needing to travel for business and thus be absent from him. Concerning their number there are four opinions. One: ten, said by Mujahid and Qatadah. Two: thirteen, said by Ibn Jubayr. Three: twelve, said by al-Suddi. Four: seven, said by Muqatil. ﴿And I made smooth for him a smoothing﴾, that is, I spread out for him life and long life. "Then he hopes that I will increase him" — concerning this there are two opinions. One: he hopes that I will admit him to Paradise, said by al-Hasan. Two: that I will increase him in wealth and children, said by Muqatil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No!﴾, that is, I will not do that. So Allah withheld from him wealth and children until he died poor. ﴿Indeed, he was stubborn toward Our verses﴾, that is, opposing.

Concerning the meaning of "verses" here there are three opinions. One: it is the Qur'an, said by Ibn Jubayr. Two: the truth, said by Mujahid. Three: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said by al-Suddi.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I will drive him to a arduous climb﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: I will load him with a hardship of punishment. Others said: I will burden him with a hardship of punishment from which he will have no relief. Ibn Qutaybah said: "al-Su'ud" is the difficult ascent, and likewise "al-Ka'ud." In the hadith of Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I will drive him to a arduous climb﴾, he said: "A mountain of fire which he is commanded to climb; when he places his foot on it, it melts, and when he lifts it, it returns. He climbs for seventy autumns, then falls down in it, and so forever."

Ibn al-Sa'ib mentioned that it is a mountain of smooth rock in the Fire, which he is commanded to climb until, when he reaches its top, he is cast down to its bottom, then he is commanded to climb it again; this is his constant state forever, dragging chains of iron from in front of him and being struck with iron maces from behind him, so he climbs it over forty years.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, he reflected﴾, that is, he pondered what to say about the Qur'an. ﴿And he determined﴾, the statement within himself. ﴿So may he be destroyed, how he determined!﴾ ﴿Then may he be destroyed, how he determined!﴾, that is, may he be cursed in whatever state he determined what he determined of speech. It was also said: "how" here means astonishment, denial, and rebuke. It was repeated for emphasis. ﴿Then he looked﴾ for means to repel and refute the Qur'an. ﴿Then he frowned and scowled﴾. The linguists said: that is, he contracted his face and knitted his brow. It is said: "basara al-rajul wajhahu," meaning he tightened it. They cited Tawbah's verse:
"Her aversion has troubled me, which I have seen, and her turning away from my need and her scowling."
The exegetes said: he made his face sour and looked with intense displeasure, like one anxious and deep in thought about a matter. ﴿Then he turned away﴾ from faith, ﴿and was arrogant﴾, that is, he was proud when invited to it. ﴿So he said: "This is not but magic transmitted"﴾, that is, this Qur'an is nothing but magic that is narrated from sorcerers. ﴿This is not but the word of a human﴾, that is, the speech of mankind, not the speech of Allah, exalted is He. So Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿I will drive him into Saqar﴾, that is, I will admit him into the Fire. Saqar was mentioned in [al-Qamar: 48]. ﴿And what can make you know what Saqar is?﴾ due to its great severity. ﴿It leaves nothing and spares nothing﴾, that is, it leaves none of their flesh without consuming it, and it spares none of them when they are restored in a new creation. ﴿Burning the skin﴾, that is, changing it. It is said: "laheth al-shams" meaning the sun altered him. They cited:
"O daughter of my uncle, the noontide heats have altered me."
Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn al-Sumayfa', and Ibn Abi Ablah read "lawwahatan" in the accusative. Concerning "al-bashar" there are two opinions. One: it is the plural of "bashrah," the outer skin of a person, said by Mujahid, al-Farra', and al-Zajjaj. Two: they are humans among the people of the Fire, said by al-Akhfash and Ibn Qutaybah among others.

His saying, ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾: they are its guardians. Malik is their leader, and with him are eighteen. Their eyes are like flashing lightning, their fangs are like tusks, and flames of fire come out of their mouths. [p. 408] The distance between the shoulders of each one of them is a year's journey. The palm of one of them could hold the like of Rabi'ah and Mudar. Mercy has been removed from them.

When this verse was revealed, Abu Jahl said: "Muhammad frightens you with nineteen. Does he not have soldiers other than these? Will each ten of you be unable to overpower one of them, and then they will come out of the Fire?" Abu al-Ashaddayn said. Muqatil said: his name was Usayd ibn Kilda. Others said: Kalda ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi: "O assembly of Quraysh, I will walk before you, and I will lift ten with my right shoulder and nine with my left shoulder, and we will enter Paradise." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels﴾, not human beings. So who can withstand them, and who can overpower them? ﴿And We have not made their number﴾, in this small quantity, ﴿except as a trial﴾, that is, a misguidance ﴿for those who disbelieved﴾, to the extent that they said what they said. ﴿That those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾ that what Muhammad brought is true, because their number in the Torah is nineteen. ﴿And those who believed may increase in faith﴾ from among the People of the Book, ﴿in faith﴾, that is, in confirming Muhammad ﷺ, when they found that what he reports agrees with what is in their own Scripture. ﴿And those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt﴾, that is, these will not doubt the number of the guardians. ﴿And so that those in whose hearts is disease﴾ and in this there are three opinions.

The first: it is hypocrisy. This was mentioned by most scholars.

The second: it is doubt. This was said by Muqatil, who claimed that they were the Jews of Medina, and in his view this verse is Medinan.

[p. 409] The third: it is dissent. This was said by al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl, who said: "There was no hypocrisy in Mecca, and this is a Meccan surah." As for ﴿the disbelievers﴾, they are the polytheists of the Arabs. ﴿What did Allah intend﴾, that is, what thing did Allah intend ﴿by this﴾ report and account ﴿as an example﴾? The word "example" may mean the same as the account itself. The meaning of the speech is: they say, "What is this account?" ﴿Thus﴾, that is, just as He misguides whoever denies the number of the guardians and guides whoever confirms it, ﴿Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl's saying, "Does Muhammad not have soldiers other than nineteen?": ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾, meaning from among the angels whom He created to punish the people of the Fire. This is because each one of these nineteen has helpers that none knows except Allah.

Al-Mawardi mentioned, regarding the wisdom behind their being nineteen, a plausible opinion. He said: "Nineteen is a number that combines the greatest part of the few and the least part of the many, because single digits are the least of numbers, and the largest of them is nine, while everything beyond single digits is many. The least of many is ten. So it was limited to a number that combines the least of many and the greatest of few."

Then He returned to mention the Fire, and said the Exalted: ﴿And it is not except a reminder﴾, that is, the Fire in this world is only a reminder of the Fire of the Hereafter. ﴿No!﴾, that is, truly. ﴿By the moon﴾ ﴿And the night when it turns back﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr on the authority of 'Asim read ﴿idha adbara﴾ ("when it turns back"). Nafi', Hamzah, Hafs, al-Mufaddal on the authority of 'Asim, and Ya'qub read ﴿idh adbara﴾ with the dhal sukun, without an alif after it, and the dal sukun, with a hamza before it. One: they are two dialects with the same meaning. It is said: "dabara al-layl" and "adbara" (the night turned back), and "dabara al-sayf" and "adbara" (the summer turned back). This is the view of al-Farra', al-Akhfash, and Tha'lab.

[p. 410] The second: "dabara" means "came after," and "adbara" means "turned away." It is said: "dabarani fulan" (so-and-so came behind me). This meaning was adopted by Abu 'Ubaydah and Ibn Qutaybah.

His saying, ﴿when it brightens﴾, that is, shines and becomes clear. ﴿Indeed, it is﴾, meaning Saqar, ﴿one of the greatest [calamities]﴾. Ibn Qutaybah said: "al-kubar" is the plural of "kubra," like "al-uwal" and "al-ula," and "al-sughar" and "al-sughra." This is like saying, "Indeed, it is one of the great matters." Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, Allah has never warned with anything more frightening than this."

Ibn al-Sa'ib and Muqatil said: by "al-kubar" He meant the seven levels of Hell.

His saying, ﴿a warning to humanity﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the accusative of "nadhiran" is in the position of a circumstantial state. The meaning is: indeed, it is great in the state of warning. "Nadhir" is masculine because its meaning is the meaning of punishment. It is also permissible for "nadhiran" to be in the accusative and connected to the beginning of the surah, in the sense of: "Arise as a warner to humanity."

His saying, ﴿for whoever among you wills﴾, is a substitute for His saying, ﴿to humanity﴾, ﴿to advance or to lag behind﴾. In this there are four opinions.

One: to advance in obedience to Allah or to lag behind from His disobedience. This was said by Ibn Juraij.

The second: to advance toward the Fire or to lag behind from Paradise. This was said by al-Suddi.

The third: to advance in goodness or to lag behind toward evil. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The fourth: to advance in faith or to lag behind from it. The meaning is that the warning has reached every person, whether he affirmed or disbelieved.
